[USER] User inquired about hearing research funding available in Singapore.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] There are several organizations in Singapore that provide funding for hearing research: National Medical Research Council (NMRC), Health and Biomedical Sciences Research Council (HBSRC), National Research Foundation (NRF), SingHealth Duke-NUS Academic Medical Centre (AMC), National University of Singapore (NUS), Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR), and Tote Board.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] These organizations provide funding for both local and international researchers through grants, scholarships, and other forms of support.  
[USER] User asked which agencies are doing research on ENT.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In Singapore, several agencies involved in research related to Ear, Nose and Throat (ENT) conditions include: National University of Singapore (NUS), National University Health System (NUHS), Duke-NUS Medical School, Singapore General Hospital (SGH), KK Women's and Children's Hospital (KKH), Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR), and National Healthcare Group (NHG).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] These agencies have dedicated departments and research centers working on various aspects of ENT, such as hearing and speech disorders, nasal and sinus conditions, and head and neck tumors.  
[USER] User inquired about agencies focusing on ear and hearing problems.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Agencies in Singapore that focus on research related to ear and hearing problems include: National University of Singapore (NUS), Duke-NUS Medical School, Singapore General Hospital (SGH), KK Women's and Children's Hospital (KKH), and National University Health System (NUHS).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] These agencies have dedicated departments and research centers that focus on various aspects of ear and hearing problems, such as hearing loss, tinnitus, balance disorders, and cochlear implantation.
